title: Views, Procedures and Triggers: Database-Side Logic
summary: Quick revision notes on views (updatable, materialized, security), stored procedures and functions, and triggers, ending with when to keep logic in the database versus the application.

chapters.title: Views: The Mental Model
points: A view is a named, stored SELECT with no data of its own; querying it re-runs the underlying query each time
CREATE VIEW active_users AS SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE active = 1; then SELECT * FROM active_users;
The optimizer merges the view's query into the outer query (inlining), so a view is not a performance cache
Updatable view: single base table, no DISTINCT, GROUP BY, aggregates, UNION or window functions; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE pass through to the base table
Mistake: stacking views on views hides cost and makes plans unreadable; CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW can add columns but not drop or reorder them

chapters.title: Updatable Views and Security via Views
points: WITH CHECK OPTION rejects inserts or updates through the view that would produce rows the view cannot show
CREATE VIEW eu_orders AS SELECT * FROM orders WHERE region='EU' WITH CHECK OPTION; blocks INSERT of region='US'
Security via views: GRANT SELECT on the view and REVOKE on the base table, exposing only chosen columns and rows
Column hiding example: CREATE VIEW emp_public AS SELECT id, name, dept FROM employees; omits salary
Mistake: in PostgreSQL a view runs with its owner's privileges unless security_invoker = true; leaky functions in a view's WHERE can expose hidden rows (use security_barrier)

chapters.title: Materialized Views and Refresh
points: A materialized view stores the query result physically on disk, so reads are fast but data can be stale
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW daily_sales AS SELECT day, SUM(amt) total FROM sales GROUP BY day;
Refresh: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW daily_sales; (PostgreSQL) recomputes everything and locks reads; add CONCURRENTLY to avoid the lock
REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY requires a UNIQUE index on the materialized view; Oracle also offers fast (incremental) refresh via materialized view logs
Comparison: view = always fresh, computed per query; materialized view = stale until refreshed, indexable, fast for heavy aggregates

chapters.title: Stored Procedures and Functions
points: Stored procedure: named, precompiled SQL block stored in the database, invoked with CALL archive_orders(30); can take IN, OUT and INOUT parameters and may control transactions (COMMIT/ROLLBACK)
Function: returns a value or table and can be used inside SELECT, e.g. SELECT tax(amount) FROM orders;
Comparison: function is called inside an expression and usually cannot commit; procedure is called standalone with CALL and may manage transactions
Example (PostgreSQL): CREATE FUNCTION tax(a numeric) RETURNS numeric AS $$ SELECT a*0.18 $$ LANGUAGE sql;
Mistake: row-by-row loops or cursors inside a procedure are slow; prefer one set-based UPDATE/INSERT...SELECT

chapters.title: Triggers: BEFORE, AFTER, Row vs Statement
points: A trigger is code that fires automatically on INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE of a table; it cannot be called directly and takes no arguments from the caller
BEFORE trigger runs before the write and can modify NEW values or cancel the operation (validation, defaults); AFTER trigger runs after the write (audit logs, cascading changes)
FOR EACH ROW fires once per affected row and exposes OLD and NEW; FOR EACH STATEMENT fires once per statement, even for zero rows, with no row access
Example: CREATE TRIGGER audit_sal AFTER UPDATE ON emp FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION log_change(); logs OLD.salary and NEW.salary
Mistake: triggers modifying the same table recurse, run invisibly, and slow bulk loads; INSERT has no OLD, DELETE has no NEW

chapters.title: Database Logic Trade-offs and Cheat Sheet
points: Keep in the DB: integrity rules, constraints, audit trails, and data-heavy set operations that would otherwise move many rows over the network; keep in the app: business workflows, external calls, and logic needing unit tests and version control
Costs of DB logic: harder to test and debug, tied to one vendor's dialect (PL/pgSQL, PL/SQL, T-SQL), and scales only with the database server
Cheat sheet: view = saved query; materialized view = stored result + REFRESH; procedure = CALL, can commit; function = used in SELECT, returns value; trigger = auto on event
Cheat sheet: BEFORE = validate or alter NEW; AFTER = audit or propagate; ROW = per row with OLD/NEW; STATEMENT = once per statement
Interview Point: Can you update through a view? What does WITH CHECK OPTION do? Materialized view vs view? When would you avoid triggers?
